nom: Good Molecules Hydrating Gel Moisturizer with Electrolytes

segments.oily: Many reviewers with oily skin report the gel controls shine and absorbs quickly without feeling greasy, though a minority with oily skin still found it insufficiently hydrating and one reported worsened breakouts and redness.
segments.dry: Reviewers with dry skin generally say it is not hydrating enough on its own and describe tightness, flaking or the need to layer another moisturizer over it, though one dry-skin reviewer uses it successfully as a nighttime hydration boost.
segments.combination: Reviewers with combination skin mostly report it balances oil in the T-zone and layers well under makeup, but some found it too light for full hydration, especially outside summer.
segments.sensitive: Sensitive-skin reviewers are split: some report no irritation and appreciate the fragrance-free formula, while one describes a barrier disruption and a rosacea flare.
segments.mature: One reviewer in her fifties reports the gel leaves eye and forehead skin looking and feeling nurtured.

concerns.aging: The single reviewer who mentions aging skin (age 51) reports reduced puffiness and a more nurtured look around the eyes and forehead.
concerns.dehydration: Most reviewers report immediate hydration and a plumped, soft feel, but a substantial group describes tightness, dryness or flaking developing minutes to days after application, and several say it is not hydrating enough to use alone.
concerns.redness: A few reviewers report new or worsened redness, including one with rosacea whose flare intensified and one who developed redness around the chin and lips; others report no redness at all.
concerns.barrier: One reviewer reports the product damaged her skin barrier and triggered a rosacea flare requiring days of recovery; no other reviewer describes barrier issues.
concerns.spots: Several reviewers with acne-prone skin report no new breakouts and fading of old marks, but a few others report new pimples forming or a purge-like breakout within the first days of use.
concerns.blemishes: Reviewers describe both improvement (faster fading of hormonal breakout scars, no clogging) and worsening (new cystic-feeling pimples, dryness around active acne) with no clear majority pattern.
concerns.oiliness: Many oily-skin reviewers report visibly reduced shine and oil control through the day; one reviewer says it did nothing to control oil for her combination/oily T-zone.

aspects.libelle: Sticky or tacky residue after application
Better performance in warm humid weather

extraits.texte: wasn't hydrating, didn't JUST break me out but killed my skin barrier & triggered my roseaca to flare up. I'm on day 7 of healing my face. (I have oily, acne prone, roseaca sensitive skin)

Disappointed… claims to be ideal for oily skin, but like other reviews say, it's extremely drying once it settles after applying. It doesn't "melt" into your skin, even though thats the entire point of a moisturizer??? It creates a layer product buildup that becomes dry and flaky. Sure, dry is the opposite of oily, but this is extreme. Not sure what skin type would benefit from using this product. This brand continues to miss the mark. Not impressed at all, unfortunately. Back to "The Ordinary" products (for the same price or less!)

extraits.titre: It was good til it wasn't
extraits.texte: I bought this to try it out because I have oily skin. The first couple of days it was doing pretty well then one time i noticed extreme redness in my chin and around the lip area. Also more pimples were forming as well. You can try it out for yourself but i personally wouldn't recommend

This product's great for me. I have a dry skin type, and this works any time of day or night when I need a little extra hydration to my skin. I dont recommend for oily skin types, and don't suggest using it as an only hydration method in your skin routine. I usually always apply last thing before going to bed and keeps my face from drying out overnight. Definitely a buy!

extraits.titre: Best For Oily Acne Prone Skin
extraits.texte: This moisturizer is the only one I have found that doesn't cause breakouts or irritate my sensitive skin. I tend to be oily but using a face wash without a moisturizer makes my skin angry. I have tried so many affordable moisturizers Cetaphil, crave, la.roche,, byoma, and countless others. This is it. It also initially is a little tacky so I wonder how it will fair under makeup. I've been using it for about a month now but haven't had energy to do a full makeup look but it sits well under sunscreen and concealer. For the winter time I'll likely go back to the Ordinary moisturizer because that, too, works well buts it's way too heavy for the summer months. (Also the ordinary lightweight gel irritates my skin, it's only the medium level moisturizer). All in all if you are oily and acne prone and don't want a moisturizer that sits on your skin give this a shot.

I'm always nervous to try a new moisturizer, I break out so easily with new products, but I've had such great results with Good Molecules that I ordered it. I'm very happy with the results so far. No breakouts, I don't look greasy 3 hours after application like I do with most moisturizers, and my recent hormonal breakout scars are fading faster than usual. I use it after the niacinamide toner and serum and it's actually making my skin look noticeably better. I will definitely reorder.

This product is unscented which is great for my sensitive skin. It absorbs quickly too. It also works well on top of my niacinamide and vitamin C serums. I wear a mineral sunscreen on top and it doesn't pill.
